title: Reading the Routes Page
content:
From Dispatch Console  :
The Routes page will display all your live information for the day.
The Top Line Summary of information displays a high level view of all syncing data.
From left to right it displays the following LIVE information for the day:
1) All routes for the day (including any manually added routes)
2) Your combined company service score
3) The current number of exception codes affecting your company service score
4) Any warnings that have been coded today
5) Total deliveries for the day
6) Total pickups for the day
7) Total number of packages being handled that day (including all packages from both the delivery and pickup categories)
********
Below the Top Line Summary bar, we will see a breakdown of all of the individual Routes for the day.
From left to right it displays the following LIVE information for the Route:
1) The route number
2) The truck number on route
3) The warehouse associated with the route
4) The assignment status of the route
5) The first/last delivery time (this indicates when the first/last package was released)
6) Stops per hour
7) The individual route service score
8) The current number of exception codes affecting the route
9) Any warnings that have been coded to the route
10) Total deliveries for the route
11) Total pickups for the route
12) Total number of packages being handled on that route (including all packages from both the delivery and pickup categories)
********
If you have multiple Warehouses or Contracts, you can filter this information at the top of the screen.
This can be accomplished by clicking on the drop down menu under Select Warehouse or Select Company and marking the data you would like to see.
Once you have selected the data, click the checkmark to the right of your selection to filter the information.

title: Modify Stop Status in Dispatch
content:
From Dispatch Console :
1.  Click on the route number to open the detailed view of the route.
2.  Locate the stop card for the stop you wish to modify and click on it to highlight.
3.  Click the "Modify Stop" button on the right of the screen.
4.  On the "Status" line, use the dropdown menu to select the desired status for the stop and click "save."

title: How to link your existing Safety Forward account with Beans Route
content:
From the Dispatch Console :
1.  Click: Settings > Preferences > Safety.
2.  Click the button “Link to Existing Safety Forward Account” which will then take you to the Safety Forward webpage.
3.  Sign into Safety Forward with the Primary Admin credentials for the Safety Forward account.
4.  Once completed, return to Beans Route and click Assets > Drivers and Dispatchers to confirm drivers have been enrolled in safety training.  You will see the statement “Safety training is turned on” under each driver name.

title: New Pins for Dispatch
content:
Beans Route now has custom pins to help differentiate between residential and non-residential stops.  Currently these pins are only available in dispatch, but they will soon be available in the mobile app.
To update the pins for your account, follow the instructions below.
From the Dispatch Console :
1.  Click Settings > Preferences > User Interface
2.  Use the dropdown menu to choose the pins you wish to use and then click “save.”
There are three versions to choose from.
Default Icons  – normal pin shape with small indicator icons on the upper right
Icon Pack V2  – rectangular shape with small indicator icons on the upper left
Icon Pack V3  – different shapes for each type of stop

title: Auto Location Update
content:
Beans Route is making it even easier to ensure accurate deliveries.  We now offer auto-updating for location pins directly from the driver app. To use this feature, follow the steps below:
From the Dispatch Console :
1.  Click Settings > Preferences > Routes.
2.  In the “Driver Controls” section, turn on the option “allow drivers to auto-update location data” and then click “Save” at the bottom of the page.   NOTE: we recommend a geofence of 500 feet to ensure best results.
Once the setting is enabled, if a driver attempts to deliver a stop outside of the geofenced area, they will receive a prompt asking if they wish to update the address location data. If the driver updates the location data, this change will be visible in Custom Geocodes*.  NOTE: the prompt to update location data is only visible when the driver tries to mark the delivery as successful.
.
*To view Custom Geocodes, from the dispatch console: click Settings > Custom Geocodes.

title: Generate MMRs (FXG)
content:
Use Beans Route to make generating MMR reports a simple task.   Upload a digital signature  in your account preferences to have the signature generate on the report. If you have vehicles in multiple warehouses,  create vehicle groups  so each warehouse can prepare their own MMRs.  Best practices include entering maintenance records as you receive them throughout the month and when entering records selecting the actual date of service.
NOTE: You can enter maintenance and odometer records on the computer or in the mobile app, but you can only generate MMRs on the computer.
From the Dispatch Console :
1.  Click Assets > Vehicles.
ADD MAINTENANCE RECORDS
1.  Click on the vehicle number to open the records.
2.  Click the “Add Vehicle Record” button.
3.  Select the date of maintenance by clicking on the date line and using the calendar.
NOTE: the date automatically defaults to the current date.  You must select the actual date of maintenance for the MMRs to generate properly.
4.  On the “Detail” line fill in the maintenance details. Click “Add Vehicle Record” to save.  Repeat the steps to enter all maintenance records.
NOTE: You can attach maintenance invoices to each record by using the “Attach Files” button.
ADD MILEAGE RECORS (ODOMETER)
1.  Click on the vehicle number to open the records.  Click the “Add Vehicle Record” button.
2.  For “Type” use the dropdown menu to select “Odometer.”
3.  For “Date” use the calendar to change the date to the last day of the previous month.
NOTE: the date automatically defaults to the current date.  You must change the date for odometer readings to the last day of the previous month for the MMRs to generate properly.
4.  Enter the mileage on the “Details” line.  Click “Add Vehicle Record” to save.  Repeat the steps to enter all mileage records.
OUT OF SERVICE
1.  If you have a vehicle which is out of service, click on the vehicle number to open the records.
2.  Click the “Modify Vehicle” button.
3.  Change the “Status” from “active” to “out of service” and click save.
GENERATE MMR REPORTS
1 .   Select the vehicles you wish to generate MMRs reports for by clicking on the row to highlight; to select all vehicles, click the "select all" icon above the list (circle with a checkmark).
NOTE: If the “Active” filter is on, any vehicles marked “out of service” will not show in the list.  To see all vehicles, including those out of service, simply click the “x” on the “Active filter.”  MMRs will not be generated for vehicles marked "out of service."
2.  Click the "Generate Report" button.
3.  Select the dates for the report.
NOTE: The month automatically defaults to the previous month.  If you need to generate MMR reports for past months, simply click on the month line and select the appropriate month.  The report date automatically defaults to the current date; you can adjust the date by clicking on the report date line and using the calendar to select the desired date.
4.  Click the “Generate Report” button.
5.  The MMRs will be generated in PDF format.  Click the link to view the MMRs to print or to download and email to your terminal.

title: Timesheets: Update/Adjust Driver Shift
content:
From the Dispatch Manager :
TO UPDATE A SHIFT
1.  Click Assets > Timesheets > Driver View.
2.  Locate the driver name in the list and click on the bubble for the date you want to update.
3.  Using the dropdown menu select the route.
4.  Click the "clock" icon to enter clock in and clock out times.
5.  Select the clock in time and click "ok."  Repeat for clock out time.
TO ADJUST A SHIFT
1.  Click on the bubble for the date/shift you want to adjust, and then click the "clock" icon.
2.  Click the "Reset Time" button and confirm you wish to reset time by clicking "yes."
3.  Follow steps 4 and 5 above to enter the adjusted times for the shift.

title: Managers: Enable Safety Gating
content:
When your drivers are enrolled in safety training in Beans Route you can turn on  Safety Gating  which will prevent drivers who have not completed their assigned safety training courses from starting their route.  Once the driver has  completed the required safety training courses,  they can then go to the map and proceed with their route.  To turn on Safety Gating follow the instructions below.
From the Dispatch Console :
1.  Go to Settings > Preferences > Timesheets
2.  Turn on the setting “Hide route if a driver is failing safety training" and click "save."
3.  After completing the above steps, contact Beans Route Support to have Safety Gating enabled for your account.  Email:  support@beans.ai  or call (415)888-9059.
Keep in mind once this setting is enabled, any driver failing safety training will not be able to view or start their route until the past due safety training courses are completed.

title: Adding Multiple Signatures for MMRs
content:
For multiple warehouses, you can create a Vehicle Group for each warehouse to which you will then add vehicles belonging to a particular warehouse.  When you create a Vehicle Group, you can then add a signature for the individual who signs the MMR reports for a particular warehouse.  To create a Vehicle Group and add vehicles to that group, follow the instructions below.
From the Dispatch Console :
CREATE VEHICLE GROUP
1.  Click Assets > Vehicle Groups.
2.  Click “Add Vehicle Group” and fill in the required information  (Name, Fedex Entity ID, ISPA, CSA, and Signatory) .  Create a signature to upload. (You may take a photo with your phone or create a  digital signature .). Click “Add Vehicle Group.”
ADD VEHICLES TO GROUP
1.  Click Assets > Vehicles.
2.  Select the vehicles to add to a group by clicking on the row to highlight.
3.  Click “Modify Vehicle.”
4.  Select the vehicle group from the dropdown menu and click “Save.”
5.  The vehicles will now indicate their assigned warehouse and group.

title: Create a Digital Signature for MMR Reports
content:
Beans Route allows you to upload multiple signatures for MMR reports.  To create a digital signature, follow the steps below.
Go to  www.signaturely.com
1.  Create a free account and sign in.
2.  Select  Edit Signature
3.  Select  Create Signature
4.  Type your Full Name and Initials in each box and select a font OR select "Draw it in" and use your mouse to create your signature.
5.  Take a screenshot of your signature (Hint: crop the screenshot to remove white space with around the signature).

title: Managers: Reorder Stops in a Route (Optimize)
content:
In addition to optimizing your entire route or optimizing specific areas, managers can also order the stops in a route one by one to create a custom optimization.
From the Dispatch Console :
1.  From the Routes page, click on the route number to be adjusted to open the detailed view of the route.
2.  Above the address list, click the “order stops” icon (bulleted list).
3.  Using your mouse, select the address card to move and drag it to the desired spot in the list (up or down).  Repeat for each address card you wish to move.
4.  Click the “X” above the list to return to the list view.

title: Drivers: Optimize Your Route
content:
With your Beans Route app you can choose to optimize your entire route or  break up your route into multiple optimized areas .
1.  Go to the Deliver tab on your mobile app.  Expand or contract the map so all of the pins you want to optimize are clearly visible.  Click the black circle with the hand icon.
2.  Use your finger to draw a circle around the pins to be optimized.
3.  Select a pin as your first stop by clicking on the pin and then confirm your selection.  Select a pin as your last stop by clicking on the pin and confirm your selection.
4.  Click the "Optimize" button.

title: Starting a Route/ Pre-Dispatch Scanning
content:
Once you have been assigned to a route by your manager, when you open your Beans Route app, you will be prompted to begin your pre-dispatch scan of the packages for delivery.
1.  Click the "Start Route" button which will take you to the Hub where you will clock in.
2.  Click the red "Start Route" button to begin the pre-dispatch scan.
3.  Scan the barcode of each package, and the app will reconcile the barcode with a stop on your route. You will see the “package reconciled” message at the top of the screen.  If the scanned barcode is not correct, you will see the message “package cannot be reconciled.”
4.  When you have scanned all of barcodes, you will see the message “package reconcile complete” and the number of barcodes scanned should match the number of stops on your route.
4.  The app will then take you to your deliver tab, where you will begin your route.

title: How to Cancel and Delete your Beans Route Account
content:
If you are an account owner and wish to cancel your Beans Route account, please  refer to the terms specified in the contract and/or Terms of Service.  If you still desire to cancel your account send an email request to support@beans.ai specifying the desired date of your cancellation.
If you choose to discontinue, cancel or terminate any Services for which you have agreed to on an Order Form before the end of the term agreed to in such Order Form, Beans Route shall have the right to immediately charge the Payment Method associated with your Account for the remaining balance due.
After completing the term you agreed upon in your Order Form, you can cancel at any time by requesting it through our support email listed above.
If you are an employee of a company that uses Beans Route and you wish to delete your account, please talk to your employer who has the ability to remove your account through their web interface.
To delete your app from your phone, please locate the app on your home screen, long press on the app and then click on the option to remove the app.

title: Assign a Direct Dispatcher/Manager to Driver(s)
content:
From the Dispatch Console :
1.  Click Assets > Drivers and Dispatchers.
2.  Select an individual driver or several drivers by clicking on the row(s) to highlight them.  You can also select all drivers by clicking the “select all” icon (circle with checkmark).
3.  Once you have selected the driver(s), click the “Modify Driver” button.
4.  Select the Dispatcher or Manager from the dropdown list and click “save.”
From the Mobile App :
1.  From the Dispatch tab, click the menu bars in the upper right hand corner.
2.  Click Assets > Drivers and Dispatchers.
3.  Select the driver(s) to assign a dispatcher or manager and c lick the “modify” icon (blue circle with a pencil).
4.  Select the Dispatcher or Manager from the dropdown list and click “save.”

title: Timesheets: Generate an Employee Timecard
content:
NOTE:  You can only generate reports from the computer, NOT on the mobile app.
From the Dispatch Console :
1.  Click Assets > Timesheets.
2.  Click the box for “Driver View.”
3.  Find the employee name in the list and click on the row to highlight it. Click the “Generate Report” button.
4. Click on the date line and use the calendar to select the time period (start and end date).  Click generate report.
5.  Choose the file version you wish to download by clicking the link.

title: Managers: Message Drivers
content:
From the Dispatch Console :
1.  Click Assets > Drivers and Dispatchers.
2.  Select driver(s) to receive the message by clicking on the row to highlight OR click the "select all" icon (circled checkmark) to select all users in your list.
3.  Click the "Send Message" button.
4.  Type your message in the space provided and click “Send.”
5.  If you have safety enabled in your Beans Route account and would like to send a message to drivers failing safety, follow steps 1, 2, and 3 above then use the dropdown menu to select “send to selected failing safety.”  Beans Route has a pre-populated safety message which you can send as is or edit as needed.  Once you are satisfied with the message, click “Send.”  The message will be sent only to those drivers failing safety training.
NOTE:  Drivers will receive messages via a push notification in the Beans Route mobile app.  For drivers who have not yet installed the Beans Route app, a text message will be sent to the phone number associated with their user profile; text messages are NOT sent to drivers using the Beans Route app.  Additionally, you can send the message to users via their email address by clicking the “Email” checkbox.
From the Mobile App :
1.  On the Dispatch tab, click the menu bars in the top right.
2.  Click Assets > Drivers and Dispatchers.
3.  Click the “circled checkmark” icon to select all users in your list.  If you don’t want message all users in the list, you can individually click on the row(s) for the user(s) to receive the message.
4.  Click the blue circle with the “chat” icon.
5.  Type your message and click “Send.”
6.  You can send a message to any driver failing safety by using the dropdown menu to select “send to selected failing safety.”  Only drivers failing safety will receive that message.

title: Managers: Time Commitment Stops
content:
Beans Route allows you to add a time commitment window for drop-offs or pickups.  To add a time commitment window to a stop, follow the steps below.
From Dispatch Console :
1.  Click on the route number to open the detailed view of the route.
2.  Locate the stop in the manifest, click on the address card to highlight it, and then click the “Modify Stop” button.
3.  In the Modify Stop menu, scroll to the “Deliver By” option and click on the line to open the calendar.
4.  Select the delivery date on the calendar.
5.  Click on the second line to open the clock and select the deliver by time.
6.  Click “Save.”

content:
From the Mobile App :
Please make sure the text was sent to you, as each invite code is unique to each user.  Using someone else’s code will not work.

2.  Click the link in the text message to get the app for the appropriate device.  Download the Beans Route app.
2.  Click the red “Sign in with email” button.  Make sure to sign in with the same email address your manager or dispatcher used to create your profile.   Your password is your email address , unless you previously changed your password.  Passwords are case-sensitive.

title: Managers: Archive – Verify a Delivery
content:
Beans Route Archive gives you access to the last  six  weeks of route data.  You can use archive to  move location pins ,  reopen a closed route ,  generate POD reports  for specific routes, and verify deliveries, .  To verify a delivery, follow the instructions below.
From the Dispatch Console :
1.  Click the “Archive” link.
2.  Enter the tracking number. The date range for the search will automatically expand to the last six weeks. Click “Search.”
3.  The delivery information will populate.
4.  Zoom in on the map; the green pin is the Beans Route location pin, and the red pin is where the driver closed the stop.
5.  You can change the map to satellite view to confirm delivery location.
6.  Click the red pin on the stop card to copy the exact lat/long of the closed stop to your clipboard which you can then drop into a mapping software.

title: Managers: Archive – Generate a POD Report
content:
Beans Route Archive gives you access to the last  six  weeks of route data.  You can use archive to  move location pins ,  reopen a closed route ,  verify deliveries , and generate POD reports for specific routes.  To generate a POD report, follow the instructions below.
Note: you must run reports on the computer; reports are not available on the mobile app.
From the Dispatch Console :
1.  Click Reporting > Archive.
2.   Use the calendar to select the desired date and if needed add other search options (route, address, tracking number, etc.).  Click "Search."
3.  A list of your routes from the selected date will populate.  Choose the desired route by clicking on the route number.
4.  Click “Generate Report.”
The report is available in three file formats: PDF, CSV, and XLS.  Click the link for the file type you want to download.

title: Beans DRO: Route Planner Quickstart Guide
content:
On average, each route you run as a contractor can cost between $50,000 to $90,000 per year, and decreasing margins is making this overhead more painful for contractors across the board. Coupled with the rising cost of fuel and other consumables such as tires, and the rising cost of labor, what can you do to claw back these expenses and boost profitability?
Beans Route Planner is a tool that leverages real-time data from your FedEx Ground operation and enables you to virtually reconfigure and test new ways of running your routes, allocating drivers, and finding your perfect balance of operational efficiency and profitability using AI that accounts for your unique business needs,  and suggests alternative configurations that can improve your bottom line.
For Example, you can use the Route Planner to take existing stops across your operation, specify driver parcel capacities and shift lengths to tweak your operation accordingly by redrawing your Anchor Areas in RouteSmart, enabling you to drop routes and save tens of thousands of dollars per year per route in overhead costs.
1. Open the Route Planner by going to Settings and selecting  Route Planner.
2. In the  Route Planner , select the route(s) you want to optimize, and select  Next .
3. If this is your first time using the Route Planner, or if you are optimizing a new set of stops, select  New Configuration , then select  Next . You should then see the stops appear on the screen.
4. Select your drivers.
Here, you may either select existing drivers from your Beans account,  OR , you can create  Floating Drivers.
Floating Drivers  represent a  Driver Type  whose parameters you can adjust.
You can create different types of  Floating Drivers  by selecting the  Add More  option below.
For example, one type of floating driver can have a total  Count  of 5 (5 drivers of this type), and a  Capacity  of 100 (100 package/piece limit per driver).
Next, define the  Shift Length  and  Shift Start  times.
5.  Flex Start  and  Flex End
Flex Start/End   allows the driver to start or end from anywhere on the map.
If your drivers are starting and ending at the warehouse, leave these  Off.
Use the Algorithm Controls to account for traffic, or bias the algorithm to reduce routes and balance the parcel volume between drivers. Once you have found a configuration that you like, you can save it for future use and apply it to different routes on different days, which you can leverage to modify your weekly plans in FedEx DRO.
6.  Optimization Parameters
Route Planner allows you to optimize for  Time, Distance,  and  Cost.
For FedEx Ground Contractors, start by enabling  Time Windows .
This will have the system account for pickup and drop off  Time Constraints  while optimizing.
The routes or manifests must have  Time Windows  specified within the file for this to work.
Use the  Sliders  to adjust for  Traffic Speed ,  Load Balancing , and  Route Reduction .
Traffic   Speed  will increase the amount of time per stop, which will reduce the amount of stops the driver can do in the given  Shift Length .
Balance Factor  will force the system to create routes with a more even distribution of pieces, at the expense of overall optimization.
Reduce Routes  will force the system to optimize the stops to the fewest number of routes possible.
Stop   Penalty
Stop Time  refers to the amount of time in  seconds  that the driver will spend at each stop. This  Dwell Time  is factored into the optimization.
Algorithm  allows you control  how long  and  how many time  s  the system will take to come to the most optimal solution to the specified parameters.
Timeout Seconds  controls how long in seconds the system will run solutions.
For example, a limit of 100 seconds will give the system a  maximum time  of 100 seconds to process the request. It may take less than 100 seconds, but never more than 100 seconds.
Solution   Count  refers to the  maximum  number of different solutions the system will process within the given  timeout  limit.
7.  Cost Parameters
You can optimize for cost efficiency using the Route Planner.
Select  Cost,  and define your cost parameters for your operation.
8.  Running DRO
Once you have set your desired parameters, Select  Run DRO .
You will see the result on the map, and the breakdown of  routes ,  time ,  distance , and  cost  on the right side of the map.
9.  Re-Running DRO and Changing Parameters
After running DRO, you can  edit  your parameters and re-run the DRO to find different solutions.
In the example below, we increased the  Capacity  of the driver to 100 pieces, therefore the total number of routes has  decreased .
Selecting  Show stop numbers in the map  will display sequence numbers on all stop pins in the optimized area.
Selecting  Show driver assignment  will display the driver assigned to each route. If none are assigned, you can use the dropdown menu to select and  assign drivers . If you are a FedEx Ground contractor, this is not necessary and should be  avoided  if you are running DRO on  active routes .
Now more than ever, finding ways to reduce running costs and support your bottom line is crucial. Reducing your route count is an important step towards profitability given rising costs of fuel, consumable goods, and labor.
Reach out to our team today to learn how our cutting edge AI powered Route Planner with its tunable algorithm and custom Work Areas can take your operation’s real time data and show you how to drop routes and save!

title: Managers: Turn on Safety Notifications
content:
If you have Safety Training enabled as part of your Beans Route account, you can receive daily and/or weekly summaries about your drivers’ safety status (e.g., passing or failing) and course(s) to be completed.  To receive these notifications, follow the steps below.
From the Dispatch Console :
1.  Click Settings > Preferences > Notifications > Team.
3.  Select which notifications you want to receive and how you want to receive them (e.g. push notification, SMS text, and/or email).  Click "Save."

title: Managers:  Adding Vehicles to your Beans Route account (FXG)
content:
Your vehicles can be added to your Beans Route account, and you can enter maintenance records and odometer readings for  completing Monthly Maintenance Reports  (MMRs).
The easiest way to get your vehicles into your account is to send a screenshot of your Schedule B to  support@beans.ai .  Our team will enter the vehicles for you.
You can enter your vehicles manually by following the steps below.
From the Dispatch Console :
1.  Assets > Vehicles.
2.  Click the “add vehicle” button.
3. Enter vehicle details and select the warehouse by using the dropdown list.  Click “add vehicle.”
4.   The vehicle will generate in the list.

title: Managers: Turn on Route Notifications
content:
Beans Route has notifications for route information: pick-up window warnings, pick-up window closed, and problematic exceptions codes (02, 04, 16, 17, and 27).  To receive these notifications, follow the steps below.
From the Dispatch Console :
1.  Click Settings > Preferences > Notifications > Route.
2.  Select which notifications you want to receive and how you want to receive them (e.g. push notification, SMS text, and/or email).  Click Save.

title: Managers: Create a Beans Route account (FXG)
content:
1. Go to  beansroute.ai  and click the “create account” link.
2.  Enter your email address and create a password.  Click the “create account” button.  (HINT: be sure to record the created password) .
3.  Select your business type from the dropdown list and click “next.”
4.  Click “select” to choose your plan and then click “next.”
5.  Enter your business details and click “next.”
6.  Enter your credit card information and click “next.”
7.  Read and accept the terms and conditions.  Click “subscribe.”
8.  Click “Launch Dispatch Manager” to open your Beans Route account.

title: Managers: Warehouses
content:
Beans Route will create a warehouse location for your terminal(s) based on synced routes.  You can then add a warehouse name and domicile information.  You can also create additional warehouses as needed.
From the Dispatch Console :
1.  Go to Settings > Warehouses
To add a name and domicile to existing warehouse :
1.  Click on the row to highlight it.  Click “Modify Warehouse.”
2.  Type in the name and domicile information and click “Save.”
To add a new warehouse :
1.  Click “Add Warehouse.”
2.  Type in the name and domicile information.  As you start to type the address, the location pin should populate with the address info.  Click on the address pin.
3.  Click “Save.”

title: Managers: Modify Driver Availability (timesheets)
content:
Beans Route timesheet allows you to set the availability for drivers to assist in creating your schedule.
From the Dispatch Console
1.  Click Settings > Timesheet > Driver View.
To remove days from availability :
1.  Select the driver to modify by clicking on the row to highlight it.  Click the “Modify Availability” button.
2.  Select the day(s) to be removed by clicking the date icon(s) on the calendar.
e.g., to remove all Saturday shifts, click on the first available Saturday on the calendar. On the Modify Shift menu, check “Apply to all similar” and click “Delete.”  Then click “Save”.
e.g., to remove a single day, click the date on the calendar, click “Delete,” then click “Save.”
To add days to availability :
1.  Select the driver to modify by clicking on the row to highlight it.  Click the “Modify Availability” button.
2.  Select the date to add by clicking the date on the calendar.
3.  On the Add Shift menu, check “This is a recurring shift,” select the time period for the modification ("For the next 12 weeks" is most common), select all the days of the week you wish to add, then click the “Add” button.
Click “Save.”

title: Managers: Enabling Pre and/or Post Vehicle Inspections
content:
With Beans Route you can have drivers complete pre and/or post trip inspections of their vehicles.
To Enable Pre-trip Inspection :
From the Dispatch Console:
1.  Go to Settings > Preferences > Inspection
2.  Check the box for pre-inspection to open the list of inspection options.
3.  Choose the items you wish the driver to inspect by clicking the checkbox.
4.  When you have selected all items from the list, click the “save” button below the item list.
5.  Return to the top of the page and click the “save” button under the enable inspection list.
6.  You can “gate” your drivers from clocking in until the vehicle inspection has been completed. To prevent clock in prior to completing inspection, check the box “ Hide route if a driver has not completed inspection .”
7.  Repeat the process outlined above to enable post-inspections.  To prevent clock out prior to completing post-inspection of the vehicle, check the box “ Do not allow driver to clock out if the inspection is not completed. ”

title: FedEx Ground: Stand up Process for Beans Route Account
content:
Prior to your standup date, you should complete Steps 1 and 2 below.    The remaining Steps will be completed on the day of standup and after.
1 .  Create your Beans Route account   :
Go to  beansroute.ai  and click the link for “create account.”    Fill out the required information and enter a valid credit card number.
NOTE: Be sure to write down the account password you create for future reference.
2 .  Add your BC and drivers   :
a.  If you are purchasing your business from a contractor who also uses Beans Route:
Provide your Beans Route Account Executive or Customer Support Manager (CSM) with the seller’s business name and all employees who will be joining your new business.    Beans Route will move the employees from the seller’s account to your new account.    Transferred drivers will remained signed into their Beans Route driver app and can see their new routes as soon as you assign them to a route.
b.  If you are purchasing your business from a contractor who does not use Beans Route, you will need to enter your drivers into your Beans Route account.
How to add drivers to your Beans Route account
NOTE:  Newly added drivers will then sign into their Beans Route app.
Drivers’ initial login to Beans Route app
Drivers will not see any route information until you have assigned them to a route   (see instructions for route assignment below)  .
3.   Get your account syncing with Beans Route   :
Once you gain access to your MyGroundBiz account and are able to sign into your FCC, you will need to sync your FXG data with your Beans Route account.    Normally FXG gives new CSPs access to MyGroundBiz and FCC around midnight on the day of the standup.
How to sync your FXG account with Beans Route
After 5:00 a.m. on the day of your standup you should be able to see the routes for your service area in FCC.    If you have synced your FCC data with Beans Route, your routes for the day should populate on the Routes page in your Dispatch Manager.
If the routes are not showing up in Beans Route, but you can see them in your FCC, you can manually upload the manifests for the first day.    Beans Route should sync normally thereafter.    If your Beans Route account is not syncing by the Monday after your standup, reach out to your CSM or call Beans Route Support at (415) 888-9059.
Upload a manifest to Beans Route
4.   Assign your drivers to their route for the day   :
In order for your drivers to be able to use their Beans Route driver app, you will need to assign them to a route.    Beans Route gathers the Star V scanner data and the route information on the Routes page in Beans Route will show you who is assigned to a route based on the driver logging into the FXG scanner.    However, if you don’t see a pad and pen icon beside the driver’s name, the driver is NOT assigned via Beans Route.
Assign driver to a route
5.   Get your vehicles into Beans Route   :
Once your Schedule B is finalized (normally a few days after standup), send a screenshot of the Schedule B page from MyGroundBiz.    Beans Route will get your vehicles entered into your account so you can enter maintenance records and complete your MMRs.
NOTE: When taking the screenshot be sure to include all of the information; do not crop the image.
6.   Setup an Onboarding Session with your Customer Service Manager   :
In addition to learning to use Beans Route yourself, you also want to train your BCs to use the dispatch functions of Beans Route and the Beans Route Driver App so they can instruct your drivers on using the app.    Your Customer Service Manager will schedule a zoom meeting to teach you and your BCs to use Beans Route.    Follow-up meetings can be scheduled as needed.
7.   Help is at hand   :
On the day of your standup, your CSM will be available by phone to help you with any issues.    Thereafter, you can reach out to Beans Route Support in three ways.
Phone : (415) 888-9059
Email :     support@beans.ai
Chat : you can access the chat feature directly from your Beans Route Dispatch Manager on your computer.

title: Managers: Generate a Timesheet Report (STD file)
content:
We recommend using the STD version of the timesheet report which gives you clock in, clock out, and total hours for each driver. The PDF, CSV, and XLS reports give only the total hours. You choose the time period for the report.  *To deduct breaks from daily hours follow instructions below (steps 7 - 9) before generating the report.
NOTE: You cannot generate reports from the mobile app.
From the Dispatch Console :
1.  Click Assets > Timesheets.
2.  Click the box for “Driver View."
3.  Click the “Generate Report” button.
4.  Choose the date range for your report; click on the date line to open the calendar.  Optional: you may click the box for “use default route length to estimate when clock in or clock out times are missing.”
5.  Click “Generate Report.”
6.  Click the link for the report you wish to download.
Deduct Breaks from Daily Hours
7.  Click Settings > Preferences.
8.  Click “Timesheets”
9.  Turn on the option “Subtract break hours from paid hours in reports" and click "save"
Understanding the STD Timesheet Report
Clock in and clock out times are calculated in minutes using military time.  Using line #2 as an example on 5/28/22:  Xavian Washburn clocked in at 7:22 a.m. or 38 minutes before 8:00 a.m.  He clocked out at 17:10 p.m. or 10 minutes after 5:00 p.m.:
8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. = 9 hours
38 minutes before 8:00 a.m. + 10 minutes after 5:00 p.m. = 48 minutes
Therefore: Xavian Washburn worked a total of 9 hours and 48 minutes.
The total hours and paid hours are calculated in 1/10 of an hour.  A tenth of an hour is 6 minutes.  Using the example of Xavian Washburn, his total hours of 9.8 = 9 hours and 8/10 of an hour (8 x 6= 48).

title: Drivers: How to Solve Beans Route App Login Issues
content:
First Time Logging In
Make sure you are on the Beans Route app   and not the Beans Maps for Apartments app
Your default password is your email address. Try logging in with that.
If that fails, check with your Manager to see what email address is set for you in Beans Route.
It may be the wrong email address, or it may have typos in it.
If it's wrong, then you can try logging in using the wrong address as your password.
If you still cannot login, then you can ask your Manager to send you a new invite link.
You will receive the link as a text message. Tap on it and select "Open In Beans Route".
Subsequent Login Attempts
If logging in fails due to password mismatch, you can reset your password with these steps.
Tap the "Trouble Signing In" link.
An email will be sent to the email address set for you in Beans Route.
IMPORTANT: If the email in Beans Route is wrong, then you will not receive the email.
Ask your Manager what email address is set for you in Beans Route.
Once you receive the email, click the link in it.
Follow the password reset steps.
Use your new password to login to Beans Route.
If logging in still fails, confirm with your Manager that your Beans Route user is not "disabled".

content:

title: Step 3: Starting your route
content:
1. Open the Beans Route App
2. The Pre-Dispatch Scan functionality should open automatically. If it does not, click on the camera icon in the top right hand corner of your app (iPhone) or the Barcode Scan icon (Android)
3. This will turn your phones camera into a scanner. Point your phones camera at the barcode on the package listed on your route.
4. You will see two things:
1. Package Reconciled (This means that you scanned a barcode that is associated with a package on your route)
2. Stop # (We would recommend Marking the stop sequence number on your package so that you know in what order to load your vehicle and which package is associated with which stop. This will save you a lot of time)
5. When you finish scanning all your packages, click on the X in the top left hand Corner.
6. Click on the hub image on the bottom of your scan app. (If this is your first time logging in, you'll have to click on Clock In.)
7. Click on Finish Scan
8. To begin your deliveries (iPhone: Click on Next in the top right hand corner) (Android: Click on the first Pin)
9. Click on the navigate button that comes up and follow the route.

title: Step 4: Choosing Navigation / Maps

title: Step 5: Completing a Stop/POD
content:
From the Mobile App :
Zoom in on the map to identify your route; deliveries are indicated by blue pins and pickups are blue squares.
For a Successful Delivery
1.  Select your stop by clicking on the pin; the address card with stop details will open at the bottom of the screen. To complete the delivery, click the checkmark on the address card.
2.  Scan the barcode on the package, and the POD screen will automatically open.   Fill in the info on the POD screen.    If you scan the incorrect package you will get an error message.
3.  Select Reason Code.
4.  Select Package Location.
5.  Take photo and click “Save.”
6.  The app will return to the Deliver tab; click “Next” to move to the next stop on your route.
For a Failed Delivery
1.  Select your stop by clicking on the pin; the address card with stop details will open at the bottom of the screen.  To complete the delivery, click the "X" on the address card.
2.  Select Reason Code.
3.  If needed take photo; if not click “Save.”
4.  Return to the Deliver tab, and click “Next” to move to the next stop on your route. Return the package to the Warehouse.
